VOIDS: the whole nine-page marking scheme was scanned and there is no award-regardless note anywhere, and no clause scoped to one language medium. questions.subtopic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation and the Photon
questions.stem: Photoelectric emission occurs when a surface is irradiated with the radiation of frequency (i) \(v_1\), and (ii) \(v_2\). The maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted in the two cases are K and 2K respectively. Obtain the expression for the threshold frequency for the surface.
questions._flag: The two frequencies are printed as an italic LATIN 'v' with a subscript, not the Greek nu that the quantity normally carries. Transcribed AS PRINTED. This is measured, not assumed: the QP's text layer DROPS every Greek glyph on these pages (the alpha of Q2(a), both thetas and both degree signs all extract as nothing), while these two characters survive extraction as ASCII 'v' — so they are set in the body font, not the Symbol font. The rendered glyph also matches the body font's italic v. No effect on answerability; the quantity is unambiguously frequency.

(i) Plot a graph showing variation of the apparent depth with the real depth of the coin.
(ii) What is the physical significance of the slope of the graph ?

questions.subtopic: Refraction at Spherical Surfaces and by Lenses
questions.stem:
A converging lens made of glass (\(\mu = 1{\cdot}5\)) has its spherical faces of radii of curvature 10 cm and 20 cm. Find its focal length
(a) in air, and
(b) when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index \(1{\cdot}25\).

questions.subtopic: Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom
questions.stem:
The energy of a hydrogen atom in the first excited state is \(-\,3{\cdot}4\) eV. Find :
(a) the radius of this orbit. (Take Bohr radius = \(0{\cdot}53\) Å)
(b) the angular momentum of the electron in the orbit.
(c) the kinetic and potential energy of the electron in the orbit.

(a) Depict the variation of the potential energy of a pair of nucleons with the separation between them.
(b) Imagine the fission of a \({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\) into two equal fragments of \({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\) nucleus. Is the fission energetically possible ? Justify your answer by working out Q value of the process.
Given : \(m\left({}^{56}_{26}\mathrm{Fe}\right) = 55{\cdot}93494\) u, \(m\left({}^{28}_{13}\mathrm{Al}\right) = 27{\cdot}98191\) u.
questions._flag: SPANS TWO SUBTOPICS, and the marking scheme splits it 1½ / 1½ so neither half dominates. Part (b) — the fission Q value — is filed here under 'Nuclear Energy'. Part (a), the nucleon-pair potential-energy curve, belongs to the declared-but-unused subtopic 'Nuclear Force'. Recorded rather than silently picked.

questions.context: The British physicist Thomas Young explained the interference of light using the principle of superposition of waves. He observed the interference pattern on the screen, in his experimental set-up, known now as Young's double slit experiment. The two slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\) were illuminated by light from a slit S. The interference pattern consists of dark and bright bands of light. Such bands are called fringes. The distance between two consecutive bright and dark fringes is called fringe width.
questions.stem: If the screen is moved closer to the plane of slits \(\mathrm{S_1}\) and \(\mathrm{S_2}\), then the fringe width :

options.label: A
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe remains the same.

options.label: B
options.text: will increase, but the intensity of bright fringe decreases.

options.label: C
options.text: will decrease, but the intensity of bright fringe increases.

options.label: D
options.text: and the intensity both remain the same.
